name: LangGraph
note: The right way to build stateful multi-actor applications.
good: Cyclic graphs allow true agent loops. State management is explicit and clear.
bad: Documentation is dense. Overkill for simple linear chains.

name: Autogen
good: Agents talking to agents works surprisingly well out of the box. Good code execution sandbox.
bad: Highly unpredictable. Agents often get stuck in infinite loops agreeing with each other.

name: CrewAI
note: The easiest way to orchestrate role-playing agents.
good: Very readable syntax. Delegating tasks between agents feels natural.
bad: Under the hood it's just heavy prompt engineering on LangChain. Can be slow and tokens-expensive.

name: Rivet
note: Visual node-based orchestration that actually outputs usable code.
good: Excellent visual debugger. The node graph translates directly to a deployable TS package.
bad: Visual programming eventually hits a complexity wall. Not ideal for highly dynamic cycles.

name: Flowise
good: Drag and drop interface. Incredibly easy to prototype.
bad: Hard to version control the JSON graphs. Debugging complex logic visually is a nightmare.

name: BentoML
note: Best for orchestrating the actual models, not the prompts.
good: Great for composing multiple custom models (e.g., YOLO + Whisper + LLM) into one API.
bad: Heavy infrastructure requirement. Not focused on 'agent' logic.

name: Promptflow (Microsoft)
good: Excellent integration with VS Code. Strong focus on evaluation and testing flows.
bad: Tied heavily to Azure ecosystem mentally, even if it can run locally. Verbose.

name: ControlFlow
note: Task-oriented orchestration by the Prefect team.
good: Treats AI tasks like engineering pipelines. Highly structured and typed.
bad: Newer framework, smaller community. Python only.
